chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Cab Calloway offers him a job at the Hippodrome
summary: While he played drunk at a club, Cab Calloway offered him a place. Thinking it a joke he did not show up, until Doc Cheatham and Walter Thomas told him Cab was serious.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So one night we were playing over to one of -- we had a friend there named BAILEY that owned (unintelligible) two or three places. And we were over there playing this night and Cab Calloway's band was playing at the Hippodome Theater. And I, that night I was standing up in a chair half juiced, playing "Memories of You" on alto. And Cab walks in and slipped and says, "what's this," you know. So he offered me a job with the band, you know. And Roy says -- so when he left, Roy said, "Man, you've got a break to go with CAB." (unintelligible), we were only making $30.00 a week with McKinney's Cotton Pickers at Carlin's Park. But in those days you could buy a new suit for $22.00.

So I said, aw, he was drunk, he was just kidding. He don't need me." So that next day I didn't go down. I told him I'd be down but I didn't go. So Roy said, "man, you're crazy, the man wants you to come down there." So I didn't go. So the very next day I was in the hotel on Pennsylvania Avenue and Doc CHEATHAM (PHONETIC) and Walter Thomas walked in and said, man, Cab was looking for you yesterday. Why didn't you come down?" I said, "I thought he was kidding." I said, "I'll be down today."
So I went down and in those days there was --
